title: Corrections and resource bounds for the arXiv v2 Trotter transport algorithm
abstract: We audit the supplied arXiv v2 of *Trotter-based quantum algorithm for solving transport equations with exponentially fewer time-steps* by Zylberman, Fredon, Loureiro and Debbasch. Exact counterexamples show that its conservation claim for spatial derivative norms is false for variable transport fields, its displayed controlled-SWAP circuit measures squared overlap rather than signed overlap, and several formulas have inconsistent signs, normalization factors, or index ranges. We provide corrections, a finite-time regularity estimate, and a coefficient-aware finite-grid commutator bound that scales as the inverse mesh spacing rather than its square for smooth periodic coefficients. This sharpens the operator-norm comparison underlying the advertised exponential improvement without disproving the value of smooth-state analysis. Independent calculations reproduce the reported eight-point discretization errors and exhibit a separate smooth periodic example whose fixed-step splitting error stabilizes under refinement. We distinguish literal equation failures, resource qualifications and unavailable implementation evidence. The results concern arXiv:2508.15691v2, whose PDF and source were verified; the subsequent journal version was identified but its full text was inaccessible and is not audited here. No end-to-end quantum advantage or general impossibility claim is made.
author: Taylor Kalin
